title: Flipkart food & nutrition growth
purpose: Learn India's health and wellness industry for a report that uncovers an insight.
about: The July 2026 announcement about Flipkart's 50% growth in food and nutrition, driven by Gen Z and Tier 2+ shoppers.

questions.prompt: What was the headline year-on-year growth of Flipkart's food & nutrition category, and which two groups drove it most?
questions.answer: **50% YoY**, driven mainly by **Gen Z** and shoppers from **Tier 2+ towns** ("Bharat").

questions.prompt: Why is this growth happening? Name what's pulling young shoppers in, and what non-metro shoppers are buying.
questions.hint: Think: how Gen Z discovers food, and what's in Bharat's basket.
questions.answer: Young consumers discover food through **recipes**, **creator recommendations** and **wellness trends**; non-metro shoppers are moving to **healthier kitchen staples** and **modern nutrition products**.

questions.prompt: How much of demand came through Flipkart Minutes, its quick-commerce service?
questions.answer: **25%**. Quick commerce was called out as a key contributor. (The summary says 25% of *category* demand; the body says 25% of *overall* demand.)

questions.prompt: What share of overall demand comes from Tier 2+ markets?
questions.answer: **65%** of overall demand. This figure is only in the summary bullets at the top of the article, not the body. Don't confuse it with **80%**, which is how much searches for healthy products grew in Bharat.

questions.prompt: What growth figure did the article give for Gen Z?
Name the four top categories Gen Z is buying.
questions.hint: One point per item. Order doesn't matter.
questions.answer: **Protein oats**, **high-protein peanut butter**, **gourmet chocolates**, **protein muesli**. (Notice the protein theme.)

questions.prompt: Which cuisine's flavoured snacks are a fast-growing trend, which two cities lead it, and what are the example products?
questions.answer: **Korean**-flavoured snacks like **Cuppa Noodles** and **chips**, led by **Bengaluru** and **New Delhi**.

questions.prompt: Which basket did the article say WOMEN are adding?
options: Nuts and dry fruits, chocolates, jams and spreads
Value-added tea, coffee and edible seeds
Protein oats, peanut butter and muesli
questions.answer: Women: **value-added tea, coffee, edible seeds**. Men drive **nuts & dry fruits, chocolates, jams & spreads**.

questions.prompt: And which categories are MEN driving demand for?
Name any three of the Tier 2+ towns the article listed by name.
questions.answer: Any 3 of: **Dhulia, Imphal, Dharwad, Ujjain, Hubli, Mirganj, Laharpur**.

questions.prompt: Name at least four products seeing strong traction in Bharat.
questions.answer: **Cold-pressed oils, olive oils, protein oats, protein muesli, premium dry fruits, authentic ghee, dates**.

questions.prompt: By how much did searches for those healthy products grow over the past year?
Flipkart's take: food in India is no longer just about routine. What is it becoming an expression of?
questions.answer: An expression of **wellness**, **identity** and **discovery**. That's the article's thesis: food shopping is shifting from routine staples to choices about health and self-image.
